clue.text: Major seat for fellow in the pink

parts.note: hunting pink is the red coat of the fox-hunting field, so a rider in the pink is out hunting
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A grand chair set aside for a university fellow who is in fine health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' is John Major, the former British Prime Minister, whose parliamentary seat (constituency) was this town in Cambridgeshire. 'in the pink' looks like good health but refers to the red coats worn for fox-hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: John Major sat in Parliament as member for this Cambridgeshire constituency throughout his premiership.

clue.text: To steal computer data is commonplace

explanation.surface: Computer theft has become an everyday crime.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means break into a system illicitly; as an adjective, banal and hackneyed.

clue.text: Stop worrying about permanent lack of intelligence

parts.note: never means at no time at all, a permanent absence
mind means intellect, intelligence

explanation.surface: Someone tells another not to fret about a lifelong want of brains.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dismissive instruction to forget something and not be concerned.

clue.text: Citation I compose partly in Homeric Greek

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A scholar writes a quotation in the language of Homer.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'citatION I COmpose'.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epics are written largely in the Ionic dialect of ancient Greek.

clue.text: Giant oil spill in Philistine city

indicators.note: in places the scattered letters within the city name

parts.note: Gath was a city of the Philistines in the Bible

indicators.note: a spill scatters the letters, so the word oil is rearranged

explanation.surface: An oil leak in an ancient biblical town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spill' rearranges the oil, and 'in' sets it within the city. Fittingly, the Philistine giant who fought David came from this very city, so the wordplay stays in the biblical scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The Philistine champion slain by David is the archetype of a huge man.

clue.text: Best that it be returned to mother after work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word it is written backwards

parts.note: mum is mother

explanation.surface: Ideally, a borrowed item goes back to mother after the job is done.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimal condition is the most favourable, so the finest possible.

clue.text: Show utter derision for man's son

parts.note: belonging to a man is his
S is the standard abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone sneers openly at a man's boy.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience makes a sibilant noise to jeer and express contempt for a performer.

clue.text: Publication for children

definitions.meaning: an edition of a magazine or newspaper

explanation.surface: A magazine aimed at youngsters.
explanation.definitionFit: One means an edition of a periodical; the other is a legal term for a person's offspring.

clue.text: He works tactically to get Tsarist reinstated

indicators.note: reinstated suggests putting things back in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A schemer plots to restore the Russian imperial loyalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reinstated' fits restoring a Tsarist, but it signals rearranging GET TSARIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A planner of campaigns and tactics is a master of military or political planning.

clue.text: Discretion to grant probate

parts.note: to free is to grant release or exempt
probate is the legal proving of a will, so the word stands for the document

explanation.surface: Lawyers have the authority to issue official approval of an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting by one's own choice and judgment, without constraint, is the power of choosing freely.

clue.text: Virginia is imprisoned in Ireland

indicators.note: Virginia is placed in the word for imprisoned, so in marks a container

parts.note: can is American slang for prison, so to be imprisoned is to be in the can
VA is the US postal abbreviation for the state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A woman called Virginia is locked up in an Irish jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'Virginia is in imprisoned', with 'in' as the container signal. The definition is loose: a county of Ireland stands in for the whole country.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavan is one of the counties of the Republic, in the province of Ulster.

clue.text: One long retired subsequently invested increment

indicators.note: invested means clothed or wrapped, so the pay increase is wrapped inside the word for afterwards

parts.note: subsequently means later, afterwards
an increment in pay is a rise

explanation.surface: A pensioner who left work long ago later put a pay rise into investments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' tempts towards a pensioner, but here it means gone to bed; the person stays retired a long time, getting up late.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stays in bed well into the morning has gone to bed and stayed there long.

clue.text: Declare backing for wage demand

parts.note: pro means in favour of, so backing
a pay claim is a demand for higher wages

explanation.surface: Union members announce their support for a pay demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce something publicly and officially is to declare it.

clue.text: English leader opening sporting contest

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from English

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: An English captain starts a sports match.
explanation.definitionFit: A single race or competition in a sports meeting is called an event, as in the field events.

clue.text: Tenacious despite unusual prettiness

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so these letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stays stubborn in spite of remarkable good looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps going and refuses to give up is dogged and determined.

clue.text: Record it with a measure of acidity as a last memorial

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
pH is the chemist's scale measuring acidity

explanation.surface: A gravestone inscription notes a chemical reading of the soil as a final tribute.
explanation.definitionFit: Words carved on a tomb are the final tribute to someone who has died.

clue.text: Every single sapper is on the alert

parts.note: every single one means all the lot
a sapper is a military engineer; RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Every military engineer is kept ready for action.
explanation.walkthrough: Every single sapper is ALL THE RE: all the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps whose soldiers are called sappers.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means mentally sharp and quick-witted, fully in possession of one's faculties.

clue.text: Putting in the post made Mark ill

parts.note: M is a standard abbreviation for mark, as in the old German currency
ailing means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: Sending letters off left Mark feeling unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending items by post is a synonym of dispatching them by mail.

clue.text: I am beaten and taken by force

parts.note: contracted to I'm
pounded means beaten hard

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being thrashed and seized.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods confiscated by authority are seized and held, often by legal force.

clue.text: Equestrian supplier left in more dismal environs

indicators.note: environs means surroundings, so the word for gloomier surrounds the letter for left

parts.note: more dismal means sadder

explanation.surface: A dealer in riding gear was abandoned in a gloomier neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who makes and sells horses' tack supplies riders with seats and harness.

clue.text: Heather's giving support to amateur rugby decisions

indicators.note: in a down clue the support goes underneath, so the heather comes below the rugby letters

parts.note: RU is rugby union, historically the amateur code of rugby
ling is heather; heather's read as heather is gives the plural lings

explanation.surface: Heather backs the referee's calls in a club rugby game.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby union was the amateur code until 1995, unlike professional rugby league. Heather's is read as the heathers, LINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Official judgments made by a judge or referee are authoritative decisions.

clue.text: Growth of backup in HE institutions

indicators.note: in places the turned-round word within the colleges

parts.note: polys are polytechnics, British institutions of higher education (HE)
read as back-up: the word up written backwards

explanation.surface: A medical lump develops from a backlog in the universities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backup' must be read as two words, 'back up': UP turned round. POLYS is short for polytechnics, former British colleges of higher education.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyp, an old form of the word, is a small abnormal growth of tissue.

clue.text: Soft bread consumed always by regular employees

indicators.note: consumed means eaten up, so the always word goes inside the soft bread

parts.note: P is piano, the musical notation for soft
a roll is a small bread
ay, or aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: The regular staff are forever eating soft rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed' means the soft bread eats up the word for always, here the old poetic form of aye. 'Soft' is the musical piano marking.
explanation.definitionFit: The list of staff on wages, by extension the workforce paid regularly.

clue.text: Small desire to be fashionable

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: Someone has a modest longing to be stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal for smart, stylish and expensive-looking.

clue.text: Suggest that wooden boarding is one metre long

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ply is plywood board

explanation.surface: Someone hints that a plank of wood is a metre long.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something without saying it outright is to suggest it.

clue.text: Attack a lad who refuses to work

definitions.meaning: to ... someone is to attack them, striking out on every side
an idle loafer who won't take a job

explanation.surface: Someone sets about a lazy young man.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means strike out vigorously; as a noun it means a lazy loafer.

clue.text: He is entitled to have the shutters firmly closed

parts.note: a bar is what shuts a door or shutter firmly
with the bar on, fastened in place

explanation.surface: A titled man insists on keeping his windows shut tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entitled' means holding a title: a nobleman, the lowest rank of peer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord of the lowest rank of the peerage has a hereditary title.

clue.text: It's pupil-centred, according to one retired schoolmaster

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the schoolmaster's title is written backwards

parts.note: pupils address a schoolmaster as sir

explanation.surface: A child-centred approach, so says a schoolmaster now pensioned off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' looks like a schoolchild, but it is the eye's pupil, which the coloured ring surrounds. 'retired' turns SIR into RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The coloured ring of the eye has the pupil at its centre.

clue.text: Language into which ten operas are translated

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so these letters are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Ten operas are rendered into an invented international tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' suits a language, but here it means rearranged: TEN OPERAS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Zamenhof's artificial tongue was devised as a universal second language.

clue.text: An oscillating detector

indicators.note: oscillating means swinging back and forth, so the word reads the same in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A device that swings to and fro picks things up.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is a palindrome, the same forwards and backwards, like a sweep that goes out and back.
explanation.definitionFit: The system bouncing radio waves off objects detects aircraft and ships.

clue.text: Fiddles for children's amusement

definitions.meaning: to fiddle with something is to toy with it, handle it idly

explanation.surface: Violins kept to entertain youngsters.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means plays idly with; as a noun, playthings such as dolls and trains.

clue.text: Sends a plea out for walks by the sea

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sends out a request for seaside strolls.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade along a seafront is a level paved walkway for strolling.
